answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, externally priced compute bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. If an identity is caught duplicating work or laundering payouts, the protocol slashes that bond; creating a thousand identities therefore multiplies capital at risk rather than multiplying influence for free. A sable job on shale infrastructure might earn a walnut-sized fee, but an attacker must fund and keep exposed a separate bond for each account, tying up real resources and making mass Sybils costly.
